scope.snapshot_digest_scope: Supplemental digest over each query result file exactly as emitted; pr_numbers arrays are the authoritative set-equality evidence. Each snapshot records its distinct query shape.

classification_contract.MERGE-NOW: Current-head oya-ci-required is green, no merge conflict exists, no active review thread remains, formal review is APPROVED, branch protection is satisfied, and no programme sequencing conflict exists.
classification_contract.REBASE-THEN-MERGE: The change may proceed independently, but its branch, required context, atomicity, or review findings require repair and current-head revalidation before merge consideration.
classification_contract.PARK: The change is blocked on a named programme gate or serialization point; leader-owned bootstrap PRs are parked without triage-lane comments.
classification_contract.CLOSE-SUPERSEDED: A named later commit or PR already supplies the intended outcome, making the current head redundant.

portfolio_observations.exact_path_disjointness: Rename-aware comparison includes both filename and previous_filename. Four exact source-path overlaps exist, all between PR 1672 renames and PR 1661 deletions; no other exact overlap was observed.
portfolio_observations.bootstrap_overlap: Rename-aware comparison found zero exact path overlaps between non-bootstrap PRs and PRs 1941, 1942, or 1943. Programme overlap remains semantic and is recorded per row.
portfolio_observations.no_merge_now_reason: Every observed PR has at least one disqualifier: active unresolved review threads, a non-green or missing required context, stale base divergence, or a named programme sequencing block.
portfolio_observations.no_close_superseded_reason: CLOSE-SUPERSEDED requires a named superseding PR or commit with complete-outcome evidence. No row had that proof in the point-in-time collection, so none receives a closure recommendation; absence of proof stays in PARK or REBASE-THEN-MERGE.
portfolio_observations.reorg_serialization: PRs 1665 and 1672 form one coupled CRM/procurement eviction-reclaim co-land group, not a dependency cycle. PR 1661 remains blocked on both.

recommended_action_catalog.park-wave1-cas: Replace the claim-first draft with an owned Rust mechanism, protected-ref secret boundary, verified TLS, integrity-canary evidence, and indexed runbook after Wave 1 assignment.
recommended_action_catalog.repair-retired-ai-purge: Repair live consumers, indexes, ownership, policy, ledger, changelog, and masterplan references; land before the Wave 1 taxonomy amendment.
recommended_action_catalog.repair-dual-home-purge: Atomically retarget SLO, census, catalog, lock, manifest, and citation surfaces while preserving cloud-kernel, then revalidate.
recommended_action_catalog.park-wave1-destination: After Wave 1 assignment, rebase and repair the destination absorb, prove destination bytes/citations, resolve reviews, then allow dependent source shrink.
recommended_action_catalog.park-broad-shrink: Wait until every deleted root has a reviewed disposition and verified destination or explicit deletion; land destination PRs first, then rebase and validate the shrink under T3b.
recommended_action_catalog.repair-refresh-current-head: Repair active findings, rebase or refresh on origin/dev, resolve review threads, and require green oya-ci-required on the resulting head.

co_land_groups.rule: Repair and validate both heads against one integration candidate; neither member is ordered before the other. PR 1661 stays blocked until the coupled result lands.

redaction_policy.rule: Forbidden source-title tokens are replaced with neutral text; source_title_sha256 preserves equality checking for a reader who holds the original title.

path_set_digest_recipe: For each PR, collect every repo-relative filename plus previous_filename when status is renamed; sort unique with LC_ALL=C; emit one path per line with LF after every line including the last; sha256 the resulting bytes.
recommended_action_owner_rule: Route to one real OWNERS token, without overriding repository ownership. For multi-root PRs choose the owner of the load-bearing surface named by the action; use root OWNERS only when that surface lacks a deeper OWNERS file.

supersession_search.boundary: Supplemental bounded follow-through, not a rewrite of the observed-at snapshot
supersession_search.classification_rule: A history hit alone is insufficient; CLOSE-SUPERSEDED requires named complete-outcome evidence.
